papers.title_in_file: A Programmable Spatiotemporal Quantum Parametric Mode Sorter
papers.version_note: arXiv:2210.16517v2, dated 6 Jan 2023; the file name carries 2022 (v1 year).
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper demonstrating a programmable quantum parametric mode sorter (sum-frequency up-conversion in PPLN) over combined Laguerre-Gaussian spatial and Hermite-Gaussian temporal modes, with pump shaping by an optical arbitrary waveform generator, spatial light modulators and particle swarm optimization.

assertions.value: The authors define a selectivity S, in dB, for each quantum state of the pump, based on the number of sum-frequency photons in the desired mode relative to the other considered modes, as measured with a Si avalanche photodiode.
quotes: we deﬁne the selectivity (S) for each quantum state
as measured using the Si avalanche photo-diode (Si-APD)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the selectivity metric in Eq. 1 and uses it for all later tables.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer lost the sum limits of Eq. 1; Table I to IV values are all in this metric, so they are not directly comparable to an extinction ratio defined another way.

assertions.value: The authors state that the information is stored in one of 3 Hermite-Gaussian temporal modes and 5 Laguerre-Gaussian spatial modes, giving 15 spatiotemporal modes, and that each is up-converted by a pump with a unique spatiotemporal profile; they monitor the output for 225 pairs of pump and signal modes.
quotes: To selectively up-convert the signal photons in each of these 15 ST modes, we use a pump with a unique ST mode proﬁle.
We monitor and analyze the SF output for each of the 225 pairs of the ST pump and signal modes.
in a unique quantum state among 3 HG temporal modes |T0 , |T1 , |T2 and 5 LG spatial
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the size of its mode set in the Model section.
assertions.reader_inference: The spatial modes are restricted to zero radial index, so the 15 modes are a small subset of the full spatiotemporal space.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pump and signal have similar wavelengths under the undepleted pump approximation, so that the inverse group velocity mismatch between them can be neglected and the system operates in the single sideband velocity mismatch (SSVM) regime, in which high mode selectivity is achieved when the pump pulse width is smaller than the temporal walk-off between pump and sum-frequency pulses in the crystal.
quotes: When the temporal pulse width of the
pump is smaller than the temporal walk-oﬀ between the pump and SF pulses in the crystal,
high mode selectivity can be achieved.
assertions.certainty_reason: The condition is stated as a regime result attributed to earlier work ([42, 55]); no derivation is given here.
assertions.reader_inference: The Results section words the same condition as the pump's spectral bandwidth exceeding the phase-matching bandwidth, which is an equivalent statement in the frequency domain.

assertions.value: The authors state that they optimize the pump temporally with particle swarm optimization, adjusting the relative phase of 37 evenly spaced frequency comb lines on an ensemble of 16 candidates, and that the same technique is used to simulate the pump shape for the experiment.
quotes: We further optimize the pump temporally using particle swarm optimization (PSO)
the relative phase of 37 evenly spaced frequency comb lines simultaneously on an ensemble of 16 potential candidates (C).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own optimization setup in the Model section.
assertions.reader_inference: The Discussion says the optimized pumps in the experiment were prepared numerically ("numerically prepare the optimized pump pulses"), so the optimization is not run in closed loop on the photon counts.

assertions.value: The authors report an experiment in which a 25 GHz optical frequency comb is shaped line by line by a waveshaper to give a pump at 1551 nm and a signal at 1559 nm, each spatially shaped by a spatial light modulator, then combined in a 5 mol.% MgO doped PPLN crystal of length 1 cm or 2.5 cm; the sum-frequency output is coupled into single-mode fiber and detected by a silicon avalanche photodiode.
quotes: The waveshaper provides pump (1551 nm) and signal (1559 nm) separately
We tested two separate nonlinear crystals with lengths 1 cm and 2.5 cm
the SF output is coupled into single-mode ﬁber and detected by a high-speed single-pixel silicon avalanche photodiode (ID100).
generates a phase-coherent broadband frequency comb with a line spacing 25GHz.
(5 mol.% MgO doped PPLN crystal)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper describes its own apparatus in the Experimental setup section.

assertions.value: The authors report a normalized sum-frequency conversion efficiency of about 1%/W/cm2 and temporal walk-off between pump and sum-frequency pulses of 1.2 ps for the 1 cm crystal and 3 ps for the 2.5 cm crystal.
quotes: normalized conversion eﬃciency of ∼ 1%/W/cm2.
Temporal walk-oﬀ between the pump and SF pulses for 1 cm and 2.5 cm long crystals are 1.2 ps and 3 ps, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: A measured device parameter from one setup; the walk-off values come from a sinc-squared fit to the measured phase-matching curve.

assertions.value: The authors report that they measured the phase-matching curve by sweeping the wavelength at constant temperature and fitting an ideal sinc squared curve to it, and obtained temporal walk-off of 1.2 ps and 3 ps for the 1 cm and 2.5 cm crystals; the pump and signal wavelengths are only 8 nm apart.
assertions.anchor: Results, Effect of crystal length on selectivity, p.8
quotes: the wavelengths of our pump and signal are only 8 nm apart.
By ﬁtting this experimental phase matching curve of the nonlinear crystal on top of an ideal sinc2 curve
to be 1.2 ps and 3 ps, respectively.
we evaluated the temporal walk-oﬀ between the pump and SF pulses in the 1 cm and 2.5 cm crystal
assertions.certainty_reason: A measured and fitted device property from one setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors tie the 8 nm separation to a limit of the comb generator, so the SSVM regime is a consequence of the setup rather than a design choice.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with 2 ps pump and signal pulses, selectivity for both temporal modes T0 and T1 is larger in the 2.5 cm crystal than in the 1 cm crystal, and that an optimized pump pulse improves selectivity; in Table I the 2.5 cm crystal row reads 10.28, 10.28, 5.71 and 7.28 dB.
quotes: We observe a larger selectivity for both |T0p and |T1p in the 2.5 cm crystal as compared to the 1 cm crystal because 2 ps is smaller than the temporal walk-oﬀ
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The extracted column headers of Table I are scrambled; Table IV (Appendix C) repeats the 2 ps, 1 cm row as 6.26, 9.5, 4.5, 4.5 under headers T0p, optimized T0p, T1p, optimized T1p, which fixes the reading of that row.

assertions.value: The authors state that high selectivity in a 1 cm crystal needs a pulse width smaller than 1.2 ps, whose spectral width is over 3 nm and spans near the peak of the phase matching for second harmonic generation, which leads to higher Raman noise; to reduce Raman noise they use pulses over 2 ps with a 1.6 nm spectral bandwidth in the 2.5 cm crystal.
quotes: In order to achieve higher selectivity in a 1 cm crystal, we have to use a temporal pulse width smaller than 1.2 ps.
which leads to higher Raman noise.
we use a temporal pulse width of over 2 ps with a spectral bandwidth of 1.6 nm through a 2.5 cm crystal.
The spectral width of such a pulse is over 3 nm
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement about noise with no noise measurement reported in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No Raman noise count rate is reported, so the trade-off is argued, not measured.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in the 2.5 cm crystal with a Gaussian spatial profile, 2 ps pulses give higher temporal selectivity than 7 ps pulses; for the un-optimized mode T0p,T0s the difference is about 9.8 dB, reduced to about 6.4 dB with optimized pump pulses; Table II lists the 2 ps diagonal values 10.28, 5.71 and 3.11 dB for T0, T1 and T2.
quotes: unoptimized mode |T0p, T0s , gives a ∼ 9.8 dB diﬀerence in selectivity between 2 ps and 7 ps pulses.
we are only able to decrease this to ∼ 6.4 dB.
for two diﬀerent pulse widths (2 ps and 7 ps) in a 2.5 cm long nonlinear crystal.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says the difference is about 9.8 dB, but the Table II 2 ps and 7 ps un-optimized T0 diagonal entries differ by 9.86 dB (10.28 minus 0.42), consistent with it. The optimized diagonal entry for T0 at 2 ps equals the un-optimized one (10.28).

assertions.value: The authors report in Table II that at 7 ps pulse width the un-optimized diagonal selectivities are 0.42, 3.06 and 2.37 dB for T0, T1 and T2, and the optimized values are 3.87, 2.69 and 6.38 dB.
quotes: for two diﬀerent pulse widths (2 ps and 7 ps) in a 2.5 cm long nonlinear crystal.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: For T1, the optimized diagonal (2.69 dB) is lower than the un-optimized one (3.06 dB) at 7 ps, so the optimization does not help every mode.

assertions.value: The authors state that high selectivity is achieved when pump and signal temporal shapes are identical, and that T0p discriminates T1s better than T2s since T0 and T2 have non-zero amplitude at zero delay; they state that experiment is on par with simulation without any fitting parameter.
quotes: we can achieve high selectivity when the temporal shape of the pump and signal are identical
since |T0 and |T2 have a non-zero amplitude at zero delay.
Our experimental results are on par with the theoretical simulations without the need for any ﬁtting parameter.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation and an author comparison with simulation; the comparison itself is not shown in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: No simulated numbers are tabulated, so the agreement with theory cannot be checked from the text.

assertions.value: The authors report that selectivity drops suddenly beyond a pulse width of 1 ps in a 1 cm crystal, whose temporal walk-off between pump and sum-frequency pulses is about 1.2 ps; Table IV gives the values for three pulse widths.
quotes: We show a sudden drop in the selectivity beyond a temporal
pulse width of 1 ps since the temporal walk-oﬀ between the pump and SF pulses in the crystal is ∼1.2 ps.
Signal modes |T0 and |T1 are selectively up-converted using a temporally optimized and unoptimized pump pulse in a 1 cm crystal.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer of Table IV reads "1 8.03 11.1 7.6 8.1", "2 6.26 9.5 dB 4.5 4.5", "3 5.0 8.2 2.74 4.4"; the values 8.03, 6.26 and 5.0 are therefore the un-optimized T0p column. The drop from 1 ps to 2 ps (1.77 dB) is small, and the text itself calls 2 ps and 3 ps comparable.

assertions.value: The authors report that a spatial pump mode X0p up-converts a signal in X0s, that T0p up-converts T0s with higher selectivity than T1p, that X1p up-converts the signal X-1s with high selectivity when the temporal modes are T0p,T0s, and that selectivity is about 1.5 dB lower when the pump and signal temporal profiles are not identical.
assertions.anchor: Results, Spatio-temporal mode selectivity, Fig. 3, p.10
quotes: we also show that |T0p can upconvert a signal in |T0s with higher selectivity than |T1p .
We observe an ∼1.5 dB lower selectivity when the temporal proﬁle of the pump and signal are not identical.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment; the Fig. 3 values are in a figure not in the text layer.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says 7 modes were considered in Fig. 3, while the caption describes 5 signal spatial modes and one temporal mode.

assertions.value: The authors report, from the 9 sub-plots of Figures 4 (2 ps) and 5 (7 ps), that the diagonal sub-plots (identical pump and signal temporal modes) have the highest sum-frequency counts, and that within each sub-plot the diagonal spatial pairs (Xi pump with X-i signal) have higher counts than off-diagonal ones.
quotes: Among the 9 subplots, we observe that the diagonal elements have the highest SF count as a consequence of having identical temporal modes.
diagonal elements which correspond to |Xi |X−i have a higher SF count as compared to the oﬀ-diagonal elements.
In Fig. 4 and 5, we show the tomography of spatial and temporal modes for 2 ps and 7 ps pulse width, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation from one experiment; counts are in figures.
assertions.reader_inference: The pairing of a pump mode Xi with a signal mode X-i is the opposite-sign orbital angular momentum pairing needed for sum-frequency generation into a Gaussian output.

assertions.value: The authors define two additional temporal modes, T+ and T-, as the equal superpositions of T0 and T1 with plus and minus sign (each normalized by the inverse square root of two), which with the third temporal mode form the mutually unbiased basis sets they test.
assertions.anchor: Results, Selectivity of superposed modes, Eq. 3-4, p.11
quotes: Here, we consider two additional modes in MUB by superposing two orthogonal temporal modes |T0 and |T1 :
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the superposed modes in Eq. 3 and 4.
assertions.reader_inference: A set containing T+, T- and T2 is not a full mutually unbiased basis in the strict sense; the paper calls these MUB sets without defining the term further.

assertions.value: The authors report that a single superposed mode T+s (T-s) can be picked against T-s (T+s) and T2s with high selectivity and T2s against T+s and T-s, and that optimizing the pump raises selectivity: for 2 ps pulses from 22.71 dB to 34.24 dB for T+p, 26.8 dB to 28.05 dB for T-p and 14.23 dB to 19.17 dB for T2p; for 7 ps pulses from 19.18 dB to 27.07 dB, 22.08 dB to 28.1 dB and 10.69 dB to 11.06 dB.
quotes: For 2ps temporal pulses, we observe an increase in selectivity from 22.71dB to
34.24dB for mode |T+p , 26.8dB to 28.05dB for mode |T−p , and 14.23dB to 19.17dB for mode |T2p .
for 7ps temporal pulses, the selectivity improves from 19.18dB to 27.07dB for mode |T+p , 22.08dB to 28.1dB for mode |T−p , and 10.69dB to 11.06dB for mode |T2p .
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment, with optimized pumps prepared numerically.
assertions.reader_inference: These dB values do not match Table III. Table III diagonal entries read 9.17, 10.61 and 5.04 dB (2 ps, un-optimized) and 13.41, 11.67 and 7.72 dB (2 ps, optimized); the 7 ps T2p entries read 3.46 dB and 2.75 dB, while the text gives 10.69 and 11.06 dB. The text figures may be a different measure (for example a ratio against one other mode only), but the paper does not say so. The 2.75 dB optimized value is below the un-optimized 3.46 dB, against the text's claim of improvement in all three cases.

assertions.value: The authors report in Table III, for the 2.5 cm crystal, un-optimized diagonal selectivities at 2 ps of 9.17, 10.61 and 5.04 dB for T+, T- and T2, and optimized values of 13.41, 11.67 and 7.72 dB.
quotes: for two diﬀerent pulse widths in a 2.5 cm long crystal.
For 2ps temporal pulses, we observe an increase in selectivity from 22.71dB to
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer lists the 2 ps and 7 ps cells in alternating order, so the 2 ps rows above are read as the first cell of each pair; this reading matches the caption order (pump modes T+, T-, T2, then the optimized rows).

assertions.value: The authors state that they achieve between 12.99 dB and 19.4 dB selectivity among two overlapping spatial modes and between 10.77 dB and 21.52 dB among two overlapping temporal modes, and up to about 26.67 dB by optimizing the temporal pump modes.
quotes: We are able to achieve between 12.99 dB to 19.4 dB selectivity among two overlapping spatial modes and between 10.77dB to 21.52 dB selectivity among two overlapping temporal modes.
We can further improve this up to ∼ 26.67dB by optimizing temporal pump modes.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author summary whose underlying values are not given in the text layer.
assertions.reader_inference: None of these figures appears in Tables I to IV as extracted; the largest Table II value is 10.28 dB. The basis of the 26.67 dB and 21.52 dB figures is not stated in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that optimizing the pumps in the temporal domain only can achieve more than 12 dB extinction for mutually unbiased basis sets of spatiotemporal modes.
quotes: By optimizing pump temporal proﬁles only, we achieve more than 12 dB extinction for mutually unbiased basis (MUB) sets of the spatiotemporal modes.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author headline claim; the Conclusion repeats it with the wording more than 12 dB.
assertions.reader_inference: The text values for the 7 ps T2p mode (11.06 dB optimized) and the Table III values (for example 7.72 dB for T2p at 2 ps) fall below 12 dB, so the claim holds only for part of the tested sets, or under a measure the paper does not define.

assertions.value: The authors state, as a technical limitation, that the 25 GHz comb spacing (0.2 nm) gives about 8 comb lines in the 3 dB bandwidth of a 2 ps pulse (spectral FWHM 1.6 nm), which is inadequate to realize temporal modes higher than third order.
quotes: For a 2 ps pulse, the spectral FWHM is 1.6 nm, which means that we eﬀectively have 8 comb lines in the 3 dB bandwidth range, this is inadequate to realize modes higher than third order.
we use OFCG with a line spacing of 25 GHz (spectral spacing 0.2 nm)
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit of their own setup in the Discussion.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper elsewhere says 37 comb lines are phase-controlled; the 8 lines refer to the 3 dB bandwidth of a 2 ps pulse only.

assertions.value: The authors state that higher-order spatial modes with opposite orbital angular momentum for signal and pump give low photon counts after coupling into the single-mode fiber (about 4 micrometer core diameter), and that few-mode fiber could couple higher-order OAM states but the spatial selectivity would be compromised.
quotes: the higher-order modes in the spatial domain with opposite orbital angular momentum for signal and pump give low photon counts after coupling into the single mode ﬁber (∼4 µm core diameter).
but the spatial selectivity would be compromised.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit of their own setup in the Discussion.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract credits single-mode fiber coupling with improving mode-sorting performance, while this passage names the same coupling as the cause of low counts for high-order spatial modes.

assertions.value: The authors report that refreshing the waveshaper phase pattern introduces a temporal jitter of about 2 ps between pump and signal, which they handle by scanning the sum-frequency counts over the delay with an optical delay line, and that each pump and signal pair measurement takes about 1 second, which could hinder adaptive optimization of the pump shape using the photon counts as feedback.
quotes: it introduces a temporal jitter of ∼ 2 ps
Our delay and SF count measurement for each pair of pump and signal modes roughly take about 1 second in our Matlab-based interface.
could be a substantial hindrance when it comes to adaptively optimizing the temporal shape of the pump
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit of their own setup in the Discussion.
assertions.reader_inference: The 2 ps jitter equals the pulse width used in most experiments, so a delay scan was needed to find the overlap for every mode pair.

assertions.value: The authors state that spatiotemporal quantum states can form an infinite Hilbert space, increasing the information capacity of a single photon, and that encoding and decoding in these spaces can be beneficial for achieving enhanced key rates for high-dimensional quantum key distribution.
quotes: In principle, ST quantum states can form an inﬁnite Hilbert space, which increases the information capacity of a single photon.
can make it beneﬁcial for achieving enhanced key rates for HD quantum key distribution.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim of application benefit; no key rate or protocol is measured in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No quantum key distribution protocol, key rate or error rate is demonstrated; the results are classical-light and single-photon-regime selectivities.

assertions.value: The authors propose, without demonstrating it, that heralded and heralding single photons from a spontaneous parametric down-conversion source be selectively up-converted by two identical quantum parametric mode sorters to obtain a single photon source with a highly diminished mode-mismatch, and that individual spatiotemporal modes could be extracted by cascading the scheme in a serial or loop structure.
quotes: by selectively up-converting the output heralded and heralding single photons by using two identical quantum parametric mode sorters
to achieve a single photon source with a highly diminished mode-mismatch.
assertions.certainty_reason: A proposal in the Discussion with no experiment or derivation in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that their earlier spatiotemporal mode-selective converter used a spatial light modulator and an optical delay line, and that its delay-only temporal control of Gaussian pulses limited its capacity; this paper adds arbitrary temporal modulation by an optical arbitrary waveform generator.
quotes: It has a limited capacity due to the delay-only temporal control of the Gaussian pulses
we overcome the aforementioned restriction of our previous study by adding arbitrary temporal modulation
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement about earlier work (ref. 47) by the same group.

assertions.value: The authors state that nonlinear-optical mode sorting techniques have an upper hand over linear counterparts because they can manipulate single photons without any loss.
quotes: as they can manipulate single photons without any loss.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim about a technique class, stated without evidence in this paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports a normalized conversion efficiency of about 1%/W/cm2 and a waveshaper insertion loss of about 4.5 dB, but no end-to-end single-photon efficiency, so the lossless statement is an ideal-case claim, not a measured one.

assertions.value: The authors state that extension to noisy conditions, namely spatial turbulence and time-frequency noise overlapping the signal modes, is future work, so the reported results do not include such noise.
quotes: In the future, we can extend our HD quantum mode-sorting approach for more practical scenarios, such as passing through a noisy environment due to spatial turbulence [37] and/or time-frequency noises [41]
assertions.certainty_reason: The Conclusion states the scope of the work and defers noisy conditions.
